import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.57

by V. A. Churkin

A set of generators of a finitely generated group $G$ consisting of the least possible
number $d(G)$ of elements is called a *basis of $G$*. Let $r_M(G)$ be the least number of
relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis $M$ and let $r(G)$ be the minimum of the
numbers $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$. It is known that $r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ for
any basis $M$. Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
becomes equality for some basis $M$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.57»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relations, i.e. $G \cong \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$
with $R$ a finite subset of the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A *basis* of a finitely generated group $G$ is a generating set $M$ of $G$ consisting of the
least possible number $d(G)$ of elements; here $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`. -/
def IsBasis [Group.FG G] (M : Finset G) : Prop :=
  Subgroup.closure (M : Set G) = ⊤ ∧ M.card = Group.rank G

/-- The least number $r_M(G)$ of relations necessary to define $G$ on the generating set $M$:
the least cardinality of a set $R$ of elements of the free group $F(M)$ on $M$ whose normal closure
is the kernel of the natural homomorphism $F(M) \to G$, $m \mapsto m$; equivalently, the least
$|R|$ such that the natural map $\langle M \mid R \rangle \to G$ is an isomorphism.
This is $\infty$ if $G$ has no finite presentation on the generators $M$. -/
noncomputable def relationRank (M : Finset G) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (R : Finset (FreeGroup M))
    (_ : Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup M)) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : M → G)).ker),
    (R.card : ℕ∞)

/-- The number $r(G)$: the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of the finitely generated group
$G$. -/
noncomputable def minRelationRank (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (M : Finset G) (_ : IsBasis M), relationRank M

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relations is finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- The empty set is a basis of the trivial group, i.e. $d(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBasis_empty_unit : IsBasis (∅ : Finset Unit) := by
  refine ⟨Subsingleton.elim _ _, ?_⟩
  simp only [Finset.card_empty]
  exact le_antisymm (Nat.zero_le _) (Group.rank_le (S := ∅) (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The trivial group needs no relations in its empty basis, i.e. $r_\varnothing(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem relationRank_empty_unit : relationRank (∅ : Finset Unit) = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (zero_le _)
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup (∅ : Finset Unit))) : Set _) =
      (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : (∅ : Finset Unit) → Unit)).ker := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  unfold relationRank
  exact iInf_le_of_le ∅ (iInf_le_of_le this (by simp))

/-- The trivial group has $r(1) = 0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem minRelationRank_unit : minRelationRank Unit = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (zero_le _)
  unfold minRelationRank
  exact iInf_le_of_le ∅ (iInf_le_of_le isBasis_empty_unit relationRank_empty_unit.le)

/-- It is known that $r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ for any basis $M$ of a finitely generated group
$G$: adjoin the $d(G)$ elements of $M$ to a presentation on a basis realising $r(G)$ and
eliminate the old generators by Tietze transformations. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 20]
theorem relationRank_le_rank_add_minRelationRank [Group.FG G] (M : Finset G) (hM : IsBasis M) :
    relationRank M ≤ Group.rank G + minRelationRank G := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality
$r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ becomes the equality $r_M(G) = d(G) + r(G)$ for some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is the least number of generators of $G$, a basis of $G$ is a generating set with
$d(G)$ elements, $r_M(G)$ is the least number of relations necessary to define $G$ in the basis
$M$, and $r(G)$ is the minimum of $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$ of $G$.

The trivial group is excluded: it has $d(G) = r(G) = r_\varnothing(G) = 0$, so the equality would
hold for it vacuously.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.57».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Group.FG G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G ∧
      ∃ M : Finset G, IsBasis M ∧ relationRank M = Group.rank G + minRelationRank G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.57»

set of relators normally generating the kernel of its canonical free-group

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.57

by V. A. Churkin

A set of generators of a finitely generated group $G$ consisting of the least possible number
$d(G)$ of elements is called a *basis of $G$*. Let $r_M(G)$ be the least number of relations
necessary to define $G$ in the basis $M$ and let $r(G)$ be the minimum of the numbers $r_M(G)$
over all bases $M$ of $G$. It is known that $r_M(G) \leq d(G) + r(G)$ for any basis $M$.
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ for which the inequality becomes equality for
some basis $M$?

Here $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`, and "$G$ is defined in the basis $M$ by the relations $R$" means
that $R$ is a set of words in the free group on $M$ whose normal closure is the kernel of the
natural map from the free group on $M$ to $G$, i.e. $G = \langle M \mid R \rangle$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.57»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ given by finitely many generators and finitely many
relations. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (R : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- A finite subset $M$ of a finitely generated group $G$ is a *basis* of $G$ if it generates $G$
and has the least possible number $d(G)$ of elements, where $d(G)$ is `Group.rank G`. -/
def IsBasis [Group.FG G] (M : Finset G) : Prop :=
  Subgroup.closure (M : Set G) = ⊤ ∧ M.card = Group.rank G

/-- `numRelations M` is $r_M(G)$: the least number of relations necessary to define $G$ in the
generating set $M$. That is, it is the least cardinality of a finite set $R$ of words in the free
group on $M$ whose normal closure is the kernel of the natural map from the free group on $M$
to $G$, so that $G = \langle M \mid R \rangle$.

If no such finite $R$ exists this is `0` by the convention `sInf ∅ = 0`; this cannot happen when
$G$ is finitely presented and $M$ generates $G$. -/
noncomputable def numRelations (M : Finset G) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ R : Finset (FreeGroup M), R.card = n ∧
    Subgroup.normalClosure (R : Set (FreeGroup M)) = (FreeGroup.lift (Subtype.val : M → G)).ker}

/-- `minNumRelations G` is $r(G)$: the minimum of the numbers $r_M(G)$ over all bases $M$
of $G$. -/
noncomputable def minNumRelations (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.FG G] : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ M : Finset G, IsBasis M ∧ numRelations M = n}

/-- The empty set is a basis of the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBasis_empty [Subsingleton G] : IsBasis (∅ : Finset G) := by
  refine ⟨Subsingleton.elim _ _, ?_⟩
  simpa using ((Group.rank_le (G := G) (S := ∅) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).antisymm
    (Nat.zero_le _)).symm

/-- The trivial group needs no relations in its empty basis. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem numRelations_empty [Subsingleton G] : numRelations (∅ : Finset G) = 0 := by
  refine Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (Nat.sInf_le ⟨∅, Finset.card_empty, ?_⟩)
  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The trivial group needs no relations in any basis. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem minNumRelations_eq_zero [Subsingleton G] : minNumRelations G = 0 :=
  Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (Nat.sInf_le ⟨∅, isBasis_empty, numRelations_empty⟩)

three quantities are $0$. This is the degenerate case excluded in `kourovka.«7.57».parts.a`. -/

theorem trivial_group_eq [Subsingleton G] :
    ∃ M : Finset G, IsBasis M ∧ numRelations M = Group.rank G + minNumRelations G := by

  exact (isBasis_empty (G := G)).2.trans (by simp)
